summary: First-byte timeouts and elevated 5xx during embedding-shard rebalance and tenant bulk-upload
description:
Issue summary:
During a customer bulk-embedding upload window, we observed a sustained increase in 5xx responses on the embedding upload route and generation endpoints. The API Gateway reported a large number of first-byte timeouts (upstream handshake/first-byte) coincident with an embeddings shard rebalance initiated by the embeddings service. Customers reported failed bulk uploads and slow inference (time-to-first-token) for embedding-related calls.

Impact:
- NovaForms (enterprise) bulk upload jobs saw ~45% failures and degraded throughput for live embedding calls across their tenant in us-east-1.
- Elevated 5xx rate across embedding routes and downstream chat/merge endpoints that fan-out to embedding services.
- Customer-facing timeouts and billing discrepancy inquiries filed via support.

Environment:
- Prod, us-east-1 region.
- Affected services: embeddings-service (shard rebalance), serving-runtime, api-gateway, autoscaler.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Start a bulk embedding upload (100k vectors) against /v1/embeddings with parallelism similar to NovaForms.
2) Monitor api-gateway metrics for upstream_first_byte_timeouts and 5xx_rate.
3) Observe embeddings-service shard rebalance logs and increased eviction/compact operations.
4) Observe runtime OOM and longer KV cache warmup on some shards leading to client-side retries and apigw 502/504s.

Recent timeline (key events):
- 2026-03-12 13:05 UTC: NovaForms bulk-upload starts (customer-reported).
- 2026-03-12 13:12 UTC: embeddings-service begins shard rebalancing (reshard event triggered by autoscaler).
- 2026-03-12 13:14 UTC: api-gateway first-byte timeout metric spikes; concurrent 5xx rate rises to 12%.
- 2026-03-12 13:22 UTC: Serving runtime OOM retries on two shard hosts; consumer-facing retries amplify load.
- 2026-03-12 13:40 UTC: Support ticket opened by Priya Kapoor; SRE paged.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: shard rebalancing caused a temporary increase in cold-starts (KV cache miss, model warmup) that pushed the serving-runtime beyond memory thresholds leading to OOMs and slow first-byte responses.
Observed correlation: embeddings-service logs contain 'reshard: moving 12 segments' and several 'compact' and 'snapshot' operations at 13:12 UTC.
api-gateway traces show majority of 502/504s are 'upstream-first-byte-timeout' with long tail of retries from client SDKs that increased connection churn.
Heap profiles from two runtime hosts (host-emb-07, host-emb-09) show transient GPU memory fragmentation and repeated CUDA driver resets around the time of elevated errors.
Autoscaler activity: an aggressive scale-out policy triggered multiple ephemeral embedding workers; they competed for NVMe and caused iowait spikes on the shard nodes.
Customer note: NovaForms client used 128 concurrent connections with aggressive retry backoff disabled, contributing to thundering retries.
We confirmed that rate limiting headers were not honored by the customer's older SDK version leading to higher effective QPS than tenant SLA allowed.
mitigation_actions: Short term: temporarily paused NovaForms bulk upload on request of customer at 2026-03-12 14:05 UTC to arrest error amplification.
Short term: applied a soft rate cap at the ingress layer for the NovaForms tenant (tenant-level QPS cap) at 14:12 UTC.
Short term: temporarily disabled automatic shard rebalancing for embeddings-service for 10 minutes to allow warmed shards to stabilize (operator intervention).
Medium term: rolled a hotfix to autoscaler policy to add a conservative cool-down window during shard snapshotting (PR merged: github.com/redwood-inference/embeddings/pull/221).
Customer-facing workaround: advised NovaForms to upgrade SDK to v2.7.1 which respects rate-limit headers and introduces jittered backoff.
next_steps: SRE to run a focused load test mimicking NovaForms profile and validate rate caps prevent first-byte timeout spikes (owner: Ethan Brooks).
Eng (embeddings) to implement graceful resharding mode that throttles incoming bulk uploads until KV caches are warmed (owner: Maya Lin).
Product: consider exposing tenant-level bulk-upload guidance and automated preflight checks in Console.
CS: follow up with NovaForms on SDK upgrade and offer a short credit for failed run (owner: Priya Kapoor).
comments: Priya Kapoor (2026-03-12 14:08 UTC): Opened ticket after customer report. Attached customer logs and sample payload manifest. Asking for SRE triage.
Ethan Brooks (2026-03-12 14:12 UTC): Paging SRE + embeddings. Initial mitigation: applied tenant-level soft cap and paused the customer's job on request.

SRE (Diego Martinez) (2026-03-12 14:30 UTC): Observed driver resets on host-emb-07/09; flagged autoscaler surge and NVMe iowait as likely amplifiers. Temporarily disabled autoscaler scale-up during snapshotting window.
Maya Lin (embeddings engineer) (2026-03-12 16:05 UTC): Put up PR for autoscaler cooldown and discussed a more conservative reshard handshake protocol. PR refs in related_github_prs.
NovaForms (Alice Wu) (2026-03-12 17:10 UTC): Confirmed paused job; will upgrade SDK and retry tomorrow with lower parallelism. Requests notes for best-practices for bulk uploads.
Priya Kapoor (2026-03-13 09:22 UTC): Follow-up scheduled with NovaForms for 2026-03-14 15:00 UTC; SRE to present findings and recommended limits.
resolution: In Progress — temporary mitigations applied (tenant cap, paused job, autoscaler cooldown hotfix merged). Root-cause draft: aggressive resharding during heavy customer parallel bulk upload caused cold-cache warmups, autoscaler surge, and IO/GPU contention leading to upstream first-byte timeouts and elevated 5xx. Final RCA and permanent mitigations (graceful resharding, tenant preflight checks) in progress.
postmortem_tasks: Finalize RCA and publish to Confluence (owner: Diego Martinez).
Add tenant preflight bulk-upload check to Console with recommended parallelism and SDK compatibility check (owner: Product).
Add telemetry alert to detect embedding shard snapshot windows + first-byte timeout correlation (owner: Observability).
Run simulated replay test to validate autoscaler cooldown under production-like NVMe loads (owner: SRE).
